mainTopic: The end of the story of רבן גמליאל's removal and his reconciliation with רבי יהושע, followed by the time for מוסף and the order of מנחה and מוסף
overview: This amud finishes the story of the day רבן גמליאל was removed and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה became head of the academy. A miracle gives the eighteen-year-old רבי אלעזר בן עזריה white hair, and the doors of the בית המדרש are opened to every student. On that day מסכת עדיות was taught, and רבן גמליאל still came to learn. The proof is the debate over יהודה the Ammonite convert, which ends with the ruling following רבי יהושע. רבן גמליאל then goes to apologize to רבי יהושע and is forgiven. The Sages work out a schedule: רבן גמליאל teaches three weeks and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה teaches one. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: מוסף may be prayed all day, but delaying it is called negligent. When both מנחה and מוסף are due, רבי יוחנן rules that מנחה comes first. The amud ends with teachings that apply a פסוק of criticism to praying late according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The wife worries he may be removed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's wife warns him that he might be removed from office, just as רבן גמליאל was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe they will remove you too.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה went home to ask his wife whether he should accept the position of נשיא, and she raises her first objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her point comes straight from what just happened. If the Sages removed רבן גמליאל, they could remove her husband as well. This objection sets up his reply in the next step.

phrases.english: Perhaps they will remove you.
phrases.notes: She means: just as they removed רבן גמליאל.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא מְעַבְּרִין לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story earlier, where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה went to consult his wife.
steps.kashyaTarget: His plan to accept the position of נשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leadership that can be taken away is risky. רבן גמליאל's removal shows that it could happen to him too.

steps.title: Use a precious cup even if it breaks tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: He answers with a folk saying: it is worth using something precious for one day, even if it breaks the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Let a person use a precious goblet for one day, and let it break tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answers his wife's worry with a well-known saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny that he might be removed. Instead, he argues that a great opportunity is worth taking even if it does not last. So the risk of losing the position is not a reason to turn it down.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: לִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ אִינָשׁ יוֹמָא חֲדָא
phrases.english: He said to her: Let a person use for one day
a precious goblet, and tomorrow let it break.
phrases.notes: Meaning: grab the opportunity now, even if it is short-lived.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: לִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ אִינָשׁ יוֹמָא חֲדָא בְּכָסָא דְמוֹקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wife's concern from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the risk but argues the opportunity is still worth it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Possible removal is a reason to refuse the position.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a short time of honor and service is worth having.

steps.title: The wife objects that he has no white hair
steps.stepSummary: His wife raises a second objection: he looks too young, with no white hair, to lead the elder Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: You have no white hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The wife brings a second worry. Her husband looks too young to be respected as leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first worry was about losing the position. This new worry is about whether people will respect him in it. A leader of the Sages was expected to look like an elder.

phrases.english: She said to him: You have no white hair.
phrases.notes: The point is that he looks too young for the role.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: לֵית לָךָ חִיוָּרָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After her first objection is answered, she raises a new one.
steps.kashyaTarget: His fitness to lead because of his young appearance.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A leader of elders should look like an elder, and he does not.

steps.title: A miracle: eighteen rows of white hair
steps.stepSummary: At eighteen years old, a miracle happened and eighteen rows of his hair turned white.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day he was eighteen years old. A miracle happened for him, and eighteen rows of his hair turned white.
steps.whatsHappening: The story tells us that Heaven answered the wife's objection with a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No human reply is given to the second worry. Instead, the problem disappears: his hair turns white, so he now looks like an elder. The number eighteen matches his age.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא יוֹמָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: That day he was eighteen years old;
a miracle happened for him

phrases.aramaic: וְאִהַדַּרוּ לֵיהּ תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי דָּרֵי חִיוָּרָתָא.
phrases.english: and eighteen rows of his hair turned white.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא יוֹמָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wife's objection from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A miracle gave him the appearance of an elder, removing the objection.

steps.title: This explains 'I am like seventy years old'
steps.stepSummary: The miracle explains why רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said 'I am like a seventy-year-old' and not 'I am seventy.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר בן עזריה meant when he said: 'I am like a man of seventy years,' and not 'a man of seventy years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a well-known quote of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from the משנה about קריאת שמע at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'like' always seemed strange. Why not just give his real age? The story explains it: he was really eighteen, but he looked seventy because of the miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [he] meant when he said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was actually old. According to this גמרא, he was only eighteen. He only looked like an old man.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic explanation of a famous line that many people know from the הגדה של פסח.

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya meant when he said:
phrases.notes: His statement appears in the משנה (ברכות יב:).

phrases.english: Behold, I am like a man of seventy years,
and not 'a man of seventy years.'
phrases.notes: He only looked seventy; he was really eighteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the miracle from step 4 to explain the exact wording of a known statement.
steps.raayaObject: The precise wording 'כבן שבעים' rather than 'בן שבעים'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the miracle of the white hair.
steps.whatToRemember: He was eighteen but looked seventy. That is why he said 'like seventy.'

steps.title: The door guard is removed and all students may enter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on that day the doorkeeper was dismissed and students were allowed in. Before this, רבן גמליאל had admitted only students whose inner self matched their outer conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: On that day they removed the guard at the door, and the students were given permission to enter. This is because רבן גמליאל used to announce: Any student whose inside is not like his outside may not enter the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא describing a major policy change made on the day of the new leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבן גמליאל, only students who were sincere through and through could enter. The new leadership opened the doors to everyone. The rest of the section deals with the results of this change.

keyTerms.meaning: His inside matches his outside (sincere, genuine)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a famous debate about education. Should Torah learning be limited to proven, sincere students, or open to everyone?

phrases.english: It was taught: On that day,
they removed the guard at the door
and permission was given to the students to enter.
For Rabban Gamliel used to announce and say:
Any student whose inside is not like his outside
may not enter the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the personal story of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה to the changes in the בית המדרש that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On that day the study hall was opened to all students, reversing רבן גמליאל's selective policy.

steps.title: Hundreds of benches are added
steps.stepSummary: Many benches were added that day. רבי יוחנן reports a dispute over whether the number was four hundred or seven hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: That day several benches were added. רבי יוחנן said: אבא יוסף בן דוסתאי and the רבנן disagreed about this. One said four hundred benches were added, and the other said seven hundred benches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the result of opening the doors: a huge number of new students came in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute is only about the exact number. Everyone agrees that the growth was enormous. This sets up רבן גמליאל's reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who argued with the רבנן here

phrases.english: That day, several benches were added.
Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵף בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Abba Yosef ben Dostai and the Rabbis disagreed about this.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: אִתּוֹסְפוּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה סַפְסַלֵּי.
phrases.english: One said: Four hundred benches were added.
And one said: Seven hundred benches.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא יוֹמָא אִתּוֹסְפוּ כַּמָּה סַפְסַלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the result of the open-door policy from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The study hall grew enormously, by either 400 or 700 benches.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל fears he withheld Torah
steps.stepSummary: Seeing the many new students, רבן גמליאל became upset and worried that he had kept Torah away from the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל became distressed. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, I withheld Torah from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל questions whether his strict admission policy was wrong. This sets up the dream in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these new students show how many people his policy had kept out. He is asking himself whether he caused real harm by blocking them from learning.

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel became disheartened,
he said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
I withheld Torah from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבן גמליאל's reaction to the growth described in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was his selective policy a mistake that kept worthy students from Torah?

steps.title: A dream of white jugs full of ashes
steps.stepSummary: In a dream, רבן גמליאל was shown white jugs filled with ashes. This hinted that the new students were not truly worthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They showed him in his dream white jugs filled with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל's worry seems to be answered by a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jugs look clean and white on the outside but hold only ashes. This matches his own rule, 'תוכו כברו.' The dream suggests that the new students look fine outside but are empty inside.

phrases.english: They showed him in his dream
white jugs that were filled with ashes.
phrases.notes: Nice on the outside, worthless on the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחְזוֹ לֵיהּ בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ חַצְבֵי חִיוָּרֵי דְּמַלְיִין קִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Appears to answer his worry from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dream suggests the new students were unworthy, so he had not withheld Torah from deserving people.

steps.title: The dream was only to comfort him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the dream's message. The new students were not really worthless; the dream was only shown to calm רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. That dream was shown to him only to settle his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in and tells us not to take the dream's message as the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dream seemed to prove that רבן גמליאל was right. The גמרא says it was not a true message. It was a kindness to ease his distress, and the new students were in fact worthy.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at the dream and conclude that the new students were worthless. The גמרא says the dream was only meant to comfort him.
steps.whatToRemember: Opening the doors was good. The many new students were real learners, and the dream was only comfort.

phrases.english: But it is not so;

phrases.aramaic: הַהִיא לְיַתּוֹבֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ, הוּא דְּאַחְזוֹ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: that dream was shown to him to settle his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the apparent message of the dream in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the dream showed the new students were unworthy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dream's purpose was emotional comfort, not a true report about the students.

steps.title: מסכת עדיות was learned that day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that מסכת עדיות was taught on that day, and that every time the phrase 'בו ביום' appears, it refers to this day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: עדיות was taught on that day. And wherever we say 'on that day,' it refers to that day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us about the great Torah output of that day and gives a rule for reading the phrase 'בו ביום.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are added here. First, all of מסכת עדיות, which records testimonies about many הלכות, was taught that day. Second, whenever a source says 'בו ביום,' we should know it means this famous day.

keyTerms.meaning: מסכת עדיות, a tractate of collected testimonies on הלכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a reading key for many places in the משנה and ברייתות that say 'בו ביום.'

phrases.english: It was taught: Eduyot was taught on that day.
And wherever we say 'on that day,'
it was that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: עֵדֻיוֹת בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם נִשְׁנֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the admission policy to the Torah learning that happened that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מסכת עדיות was taught that day, and 'בו ביום' always refers to it.

steps.title: Every open question was settled, and רבן גמליאל kept attending
steps.stepSummary: Every pending הלכה was resolved that day, and רבן גמליאל did not stay away from the בית המדרש for even a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was no הלכה left undecided in the בית המדרש that they did not explain. And even רבן גמליאל did not keep himself away from the בית המדרש even for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section by describing how productive that day was and how רבן גמליאל behaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With so many students present, every open question was settled. Even though רבן גמליאל had just been removed, he did not stay home in protest. He joined the learning as one of the Sages.
steps.whatToRemember: That day was a high point of Torah learning, and רבן גמליאל showed humility by continuing to learn with everyone.

phrases.english: And there was no halakha
that was pending in the study hall
that they did not explain.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לֹא מָנַע עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: And even Rabban Gamliel did not hold himself back
from the study hall even for one moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא הָיְתָה הֲלָכָה שֶׁהָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 11 and closes the description of that day.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: That day settled every open הלכה, and רבן גמליאל humbly kept participating in the learning.

steps.title: An Ammonite convert asks his status on that day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as proof that רבן גמליאל was in the בית המדרש. On that day, יהודה the Ammonite convert asked whether he may enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: On that day, יהודה, an Ammonite convert, came before them in the בית המדרש. He said to them: What is my status regarding entering the congregation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up step 12, which said that רבן גמליאל did not leave the בית המדרש even for a moment. This step only sets up the case. The proof becomes clear in the next steps, when רבן גמליאל speaks in the debate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דתנן tells us that a proof is coming from a משנה. The story happened 'on that day,' the same day רבן גמליאל was removed from leading the academy. If רבן גמליאל argues in this debate, then he must have been present.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a מִשְׁנָה). This word introduces a source being quoted.
A convert who comes from the nation of עַמּוֹן
To enter the congregation. This means to marry a Jewish woman of normal lineage.

steps.confusionAlert: 'לבא בקהל' does NOT mean entering a building or joining a group of people. Here it means marrying into the Jewish people. יהודה was already a גר. His question was only about whom he may marry.

phrases.english: As we learned: On that day
phrases.notes: Links back to step 11's rule that 'בו ביום' refers to this day

phrases.english: Yehuda, an Ammonite convert, came
before them in the study hall.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: מָה אֲנִי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל?
phrases.english: He said to them: What am I (what is my status) regarding entering the congregation?
phrases.notes: Meaning: may I marry a Jewish woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם בָּא יְהוּדָה גֵּר עַמּוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to prove step 12's claim that רבן גמליאל stayed in the בית המדרש
steps.raayaObject: That רבן גמליאל did not stay away from the בית המדרש on that day
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (in מסכת ידים) recording the debate about יהודה גר עמוני on that day

steps.title: Two opposite rulings: forbidden or permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rules that the convert is forbidden to marry into the קהל, and רבי יהושע rules that he is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: You are forbidden to enter the congregation. רבי יהושע said to him: You are permitted to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The two great sages give opposite answers to the convert. This sets up the debate in the next steps, where each one defends his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here we already see that רבן גמליאל is present and taking part. That is the core of the proof. The rest of the debate explains the reasoning behind each side.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him:
You are forbidden to enter the congregation.
Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
You are permitted to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אָסוּר אַתָּה לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the convert's question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל forbids the convert to marry into the קהל. רבי יהושע permits it.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל challenges from the Torah's ban on עמונים
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי יהושע with the פסוק that says an Ammonite may not enter the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But it is already written: 'An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל attacks רבי יהושע's lenient ruling by quoting an explicit פסוק in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah clearly forbids an עמוני to marry into the Jewish people. So how can רבי יהושע permit a man who is an Ammonite convert?

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not already stated? This phrase introduces a challenge from a פָּסוּק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him: But was it not already stated:
"An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע's lenient ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that the Ammonite convert is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah פסוק explicitly bans עמוני from the קהל.

steps.title: Sennacherib mixed up the nations, so we follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that סנחריב scrambled all the nations, so today's residents of עמון are not true Ammonites. A person who separates from a mixed group is assumed to come from the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Do עמון and מואב still live in their original place? סנחריב king of Assyria already came up and mixed up all the nations, as it says: 'I have removed the borders of peoples, and robbed their treasures, and brought down the mighty inhabitants.' And anyone who separates from a group is assumed to separate from the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע defends his ruling. The פסוק is true, but the people living in עמון today are not real Ammonites.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סנחריב moved whole nations around, so the people of each land became mixed. Most of the world is not Ammonite. So by the rule 'כל דפריש מרובא פריש,' this convert is treated as coming from the permitted majority.

keyTerms.meaning: The king of אַשּׁוּר (Assyria) who exiled and moved whole nations
Whatever separates from a group is assumed to come from the majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the rule that the Torah's ban on עמוני and מצרי no longer applies in practice, because the nations have been mixed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין?
phrases.english: Do Ammon and Moab still dwell in their place?
Sennacherib king of Assyria already came up
and mixed up all the nations,
as it is stated: "I have removed the borders of peoples
and robbed their treasures
and brought down, as a mighty one, the inhabitants",
and whatever separates, separates from the majority.
phrases.notes: So the convert is assumed to come from the permitted majority of nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's challenge from the פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual reality changed. The Torah's category still exists, but we cannot identify who belongs to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The convert from עמון is a real Ammonite, so the פסוק forbids him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the nations were mixed, he is presumed to come from the permitted majority.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the עמונים were promised a return and already returned
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל counters with a prophecy that עמון would return to its land, and says it has already happened, so the Ammonites are back in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But it is already written: 'And afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of עמון, says ה׳.' And they have already returned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל attacks רבי יהושע's answer. He argues that the Ammonites went back home after סנחריב's mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Ammonites returned to their land, then the people of עמון today are real Ammonites again. That would cancel רבי יהושע's argument about mixing.

keyTerms.meaning: Captivity, or exiles who are brought back

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to him: But was it not already stated:
"And afterward I will bring back the captivity
of the children of Ammon, says the Lord",
and they have already returned!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אָשִׁיב אֶת שְׁבוּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהושע's argument about mixing
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that the Ammonites are no longer in their place
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A prophecy promised the Ammonites would return, so they are assumed to be back and identifiable.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a promise is not proof it already happened
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the proof. Israel was also promised a return and has not yet returned, so a prophecy does not prove that something already happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But it is already written: 'And I will return the captivity of My people Israel,' and they have not yet returned!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back on רבן גמליאל's proof using a similar prophecy about Israel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A prophecy tells us what will happen someday, not that it has already happened. Israel's promised return has not happened yet. So we cannot assume that עמון's return has happened either, and a ruling must rest on known facts.

keyTerms.meaning: And they have still not returned

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: But was it not already stated:
"And I will return the captivity of My people Israel",
and they have not yet returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְשַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁבוּת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבן גמליאל's proof from the prophecy about עמון
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from ירמיהו's prophecy that the Ammonites already returned
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A prophecy of return does not show the return already happened. Israel's parallel prophecy has not yet come true.

steps.title: The convert is permitted right away
steps.stepSummary: The sages immediately permitted יהודה the Ammonite convert to marry into the קהל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately they permitted him to enter the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate ends with a final ruling that follows רבי יהושע: the convert may marry a Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע. This also finishes the proof for step 12. רבן גמליאל was actively debating in the בית המדרש that day, so he clearly did not stay away.
steps.whatToRemember: On the day רבן גמליאל was removed, he still came and argued in the בית המדרש. The convert was permitted because סנחריב mixed the nations, so we follow the majority (כל דפריש מרובא פריש).

phrases.english: Immediately they permitted him to enter the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד הִתִּירוּהוּ לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final ruling after רבי יהושע's rejection of רבן גמליאל's proof
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The Ammonite convert is permitted to marry into the קהל, following רבי יהושע. Because רבן גמליאל took part in the debate, this proves he was present in the בית המדרש that day.

steps.title: A visit to make peace
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל decides to apologize to רבי יהושע and notices the dark walls of his home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says he will go and appease רבי יהושע. When he arrives, he sees that the walls of the house are blackened.
steps.whatsHappening: The text begins a new episode. רבן גמליאל goes to רבי יהושע’s home to make peace, and the walls catch his attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase הואיל והכי הוה ('since this is how it turned out') points back to the debate that just ended. The בית המדרש ruled like רבי יהושע and against רבן גמליאל, so רבן גמליאל saw that רבי יהושע had the Sages' support and decided to make peace. The dark walls set up the exchange that follows.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: הוֹאִיל וְהָכִי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said: Since this is what happened,
I will go and appease Rabbi Yehoshua.
When he reached his house,
he saw that the walls of his house were blackened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: הוֹאִיל וְהָכִי הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the main story. The ruling in step 19, which followed רבי יהושע, is what prompts רבן גמליאל to go and appease him ('הואיל והכי הוה').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל resolves to seek רבי יהושע’s forgiveness.

steps.title: The walls reveal an overlooked hardship
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל comments on רבי יהושע’s work; רבי יהושע responds that a leader should know how scholars support themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says the walls show that רבי יהושע works with charcoal. רבי יהושע replies: Woe to a generation whose leader does not know the hardship of Torah scholars or how they earn a living and find food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל connects the blackened walls to רבי יהושע’s work. רבי יהושע turns that observation into a sharp criticism of his leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether the walls are dark. רבי יהושע is saying that רבן גמליאל has not understood the daily struggles of the scholars he leads.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִכּוֹתְלֵי בֵיתְךָ אַתָּה נִיכָּר
phrases.english: He said to him: From the walls of your house it is clear
that you are a charcoal worker.
He said to him: Woe to the generation
of which you are the leader,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ בְּצַעֲרָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: for you do not know the hardship of Torah scholars,

phrases.aramaic: בַּמֶּה הֵם מִתְפַּרְנְסִים וּבַמֶּה הֵם נִזּוֹנִים.
phrases.english: how they support themselves and how they obtain food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹי לוֹ לַדּוֹר שֶׁאַתָּה פַּרְנָסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The walls noticed in step 20 lead to רבי יהושע’s criticism.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל’s understanding of the scholars he leads.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His surprise at רבי יהושע’s work shows that he has not known about their hardship.

steps.title: The apology is accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל apologizes; רבי יהושע initially ignores him but is then appeased.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says, “I have wronged you; forgive me.” רבי יהושע does not respond. רבן גמליאל asks him to do it for his father’s honor, and רבי יהושע is appeased.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל asks for forgiveness. His first request fails, but the appeal to his father’s honor succeeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word “appeased” settles their personal exchange. It does not yet say what will happen to leadership in the בית מדרש; the next lines take that up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נַעֲנֵיתִי לְךָ מְחוֹל לִי.
phrases.english: He said to him: I wronged you; forgive me.
He paid him no attention.
Do it for my father’s honor.
He was appeased.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּיֵּיס.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The criticism is followed by an apology and personal reconciliation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע accepts the appeal and is appeased.

steps.title: Who will tell the scholars?
steps.stepSummary: The group asks who will inform the חכמים, and a launderer volunteers.
steps.simpleTranslation: They ask, “Who will go and tell the Sages?” A certain launderer says, “I will go.”
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי יהושע is appeased, the group needs to send word to the חכמים. This question sets up the message that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The text does not yet say what the message will be. It first identifies someone willing to carry it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ: מַאן נֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: They said: Who will go and tell the Sages?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ הַהוּא כּוֹבֵס: אֲנָא אָזֵילְנָא.
phrases.english: A certain launderer said to them: I will go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ: מַאן נֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Personal reconciliation creates a need to inform the בית מדרש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who will deliver word to the חכמים?

steps.title: The one wearing the uniform should keep it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע sends the בית מדרש a comparison: someone already wearing a uniform should not be told to hand it over to someone who was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע sends word to the study hall: Let the one who wears the uniform wear it. Should someone who does not wear it tell the wearer, “Send me your uniform, and I will wear it”?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע sends his message through an image of a uniform. He is preparing the חכמים to reconsider who should hold the leadership position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question at the end is rhetorical: it objects to taking the uniform from its wearer. In this setting, the uniform stands for the leadership position previously held by רבן גמליאל.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua sent word to them at the study hall:
The one who wears the uniform should wear the uniform,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּלָא לָבֵישׁ מַדָּא יֵימַר לֵיהּ
phrases.english: and should one who does not wear the uniform say
to the one who wears the uniform:
Send me your uniform, and I will wear it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The message anticipated in step 23 is delivered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע argues, through the uniform image, for retaining the earlier holder of the leadership position.

steps.title: Protect the study hall from pressure
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tells the חכמים to lock the gates so רבן גמליאל’s servants cannot trouble them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא tells the Sages: Lock the gates so that רבן גמליאל’s servants do not come and trouble the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא responds to the message with a protective instruction. He wants the gates closed against possible pressure on the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages seem to have assumed that the launderer's message really came from רבן גמליאל's side, not from רבי יהושע. So רבי עקיבא shuts the gates against רבן גמליאל's people instead of acting on the message. This is why רבי יהושע must come in person in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to the Sages:
Lock the gates,
so that Rabban Gamliel’s servants do not come
and trouble the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבָּנַן: טְרוּקוּ גַּלֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The message is followed by an instruction to guard the בית מדרש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא instructs the חכמים to close the gates against possible interference.

steps.title: רבי יהושע speaks for himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע goes to the חכמים and gives a second comparison, this time about someone authorized to sprinkle purification water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says it is better that he go to them himself. He comes, knocks, and says: Let one who sprinkles, the son of one who sprinkles, continue to sprinkle. Should someone who is neither a sprinkler nor the son of one tell him that his water and ashes are invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע goes to the closed door himself. He restates his point with a new image, challenging the idea that an outsider should dismiss an established holder of a role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the image, the criticism about cave water and burnt ashes would disqualify the sprinkler’s materials. רבי יהושע uses it to make the objection sound unfair; he is not deciding a case about actual purification water here.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מוּטָב דְּאֵיקוּם וְאֵיזִיל אֲנָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: It is better that I get up and go
to them myself.
He came, knocked on the door, and said to them:
One who sprinkles, the son of one who sprinkles, should sprinkle.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא מַזֶּה וְלֹא בֶּן מַזֶּה
phrases.english: And should one who is neither a sprinkler nor the son of one
say to a sprinkler, the son of a sprinkler,

phrases.aramaic: מֵימֶיךָ מֵי מְעָרָה וְאֶפְרְךָ אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה.
phrases.english: Your water is cave water, and your ashes are ordinary burnt ash?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מוּטָב דְּאֵיקוּם וְאֵיזִיל אֲנָא לְגַבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the instruction to close the gates, רבי יהושע comes in person to make his meaning clear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע presses his argument against displacing the earlier leader.

steps.title: They will approach רבן גמליאל together
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא checks that רבי יהושע is appeased, explains why the חכמים acted, and proposes going together the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא asks רבי יהושע whether he has been appeased. He says they acted only for רבי יהושע’s honor, and proposes that the two of them go to רבן גמליאל’s doorway early the next morning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא makes sure that רבי יהושע’s forgiveness is real. He then proposes a joint visit for the following morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His explanation links the חכמים’s actions to concern for רבי יהושע’s honor. Now that רבי יהושע is appeased, they plan to go to רבן גמליאל. Steps 28–29 work out the new leadership arrangement.
steps.whatToRemember: Once רבי יהושע is truly appeased, the Sages agree to restore רבן גמליאל. Steps 28–29 work out what happens to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, נִתְפַּיַּיסְתָּ?
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: Rabbi Yehoshua, have you been appeased?
Did we do anything except act for your honor?
Tomorrow you and I will go early to his doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, נִתְפַּיַּיסְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא responds to רבי יהושע’s personal arrival and words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהושע plan to approach רבן גמליאל together the next morning to restore him. Steps 28–29 settle the resulting leadership arrangement.

steps.title: Two possible schedules, two problems
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים consider removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה or giving each leader an equal turn, but find a problem with each plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: What should we do? Remove him? We have learned that one raises a person in sanctity and does not lower him. Should each one teach one week? They may become jealous.
steps.whatsHappening: After the plan to bring רבן גמליאל back, the חכמים work through what to do about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. This discussion sets up a third arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would lower him from a position he already holds. Giving the two leaders equal, alternating weeks could create rivalry.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us remove him from his position.
They may come to be jealous.

phrases.english: They said: What should we do? Remove him?
We have learned: One raises in sanctity and does not lower.
Should one master teach one week
and the other master one week? They may become jealous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הֵיכִי נַעֲבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The proposed reconciliation now needs a workable teaching schedule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can רבן גמליאל return without improperly removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה or creating rivalry?

steps.title: A three-to-one teaching schedule
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים settle on three weeks for רבן גמליאל and one for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let רבן גמליאל teach for three weeks and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה for one week.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים choose a schedule that gives רבן גמליאל most weeks while keeping רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in a teaching role.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids removing רבי אלעזר בן עזריה altogether. It also avoids the equal, week-by-week alternation that concerned them.
steps.whatToRemember: The solution is a three-to-one schedule, not the removal of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: Rather, let Rabban Gamliel teach

phrases.aramaic: תְּלָתָא שַׁבָּתֵי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: for three weeks, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
for one week.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לִדְרוֹשׁ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It replaces the two rejected schedules with a compromise.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן גמליאל teaches three weeks out of four; רבי אלעזר בן עזריה teaches the fourth.

steps.title: A reference to one week and the student’s identity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the schedule to a reference to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה’s week, then identifies the student from the earlier incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what was meant by the statement, “Whose week was it? It was רבי אלעזר בן עזריה’s.” And that student was רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a later reference that fits the new schedule. It then adds one last detail about the student in the earlier story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A week could now be called רבי אלעזר בן עזריה’s week because he taught once every four weeks. The student who asked the question that began the incident is identified as רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is meant.
The student identified at the end of the story.

phrases.english: And this is what the master meant when he said:
Whose week was it?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הָיְתָה.
phrases.english: It was Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya’s.

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי הֲוָה.
phrases.english: And that student was Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The agreed schedule explains why a particular week belonged to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The time for מוסף and a warning about delay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the rule that מוסף may be prayed all day, and רבי יוחנן warns against delaying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מוסף may be recited all day. רבי יוחנן said: Nevertheless, one who delays it is called negligent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the leadership story and returns to the earlier rule about the time for מוסף. רבי יוחנן adds a warning about waiting too long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “All day” describes the available time for מוסף. It does not mean that delaying it is a good choice.

phrases.english: And the additional prayer may be recited all day.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And he is called “negligent.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The narrative ends, and the גמרא resumes its discussion of תפילה times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although מוסף can be recited all day, excessive delay is called negligent.

steps.title: The first view puts מנחה before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when both תפילות are due, מנחה comes first because it is more frequent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a person has two תפילות before him, one מנחה and one מוסף, he prays מנחה and then מוסף, because this one is frequent and that one is not frequent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a ברייתא about someone who still needs to pray both מנחה and מוסף. Its first view gives priority to מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה is prayed every day, while מוסף is prayed only on particular days. This view uses frequency to decide the order when both are waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If he has two prayers before him,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל מִנְחָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל מוּסָף —
phrases.english: one the afternoon prayer and one the additional prayer,
he prays the afternoon prayer and afterward
prays the additional prayer, for this one is frequent,
and this one is not frequent.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing how late מוסף can be prayed, the גמרא considers its order relative to מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both are due, pray מנחה before מוסף because מנחה is more frequent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה puts מוסף first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives the opposite order because, in his view, the time for מוסף will end sooner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He prays מוסף and afterward מנחה, because this one is a מצוה whose time is passing, and this one is a מצוה whose time is not passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents רבי יהודה’s differing view. He puts מוסף before מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה focuses on which תפילה is at greater risk of running out of time. In his view, מוסף has the earlier deadline, so it goes first despite being less frequent.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who gives the opposing order here.
A מצוה whose available time is passing.
A מצוה whose available time is not yet passing.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁל מוּסָף
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He prays the additional prayer
and afterward prays the afternoon prayer,
because this one is a מצוה whose time is passing,
and this one is a מצוה whose time is not passing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה disputes the first view’s ordering by using a different priority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pray מוסף before מנחה when both are due, because מוסף has the earlier deadline in רבי יהודה’s view.

steps.title: The ruling puts מנחה first
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that מנחה is prayed before מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is that he prays מנחה and afterward prays מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן states which order to follow. He rules like the first view in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this case, the ruling gives priority to the more frequent תפילה, מנחה. The earlier-deadline argument of רבי יהודה does not determine the ruling here.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who states the ruling.

steps.whatToRemember: When both מנחה and מוסף are before him, the ruling stated here is מנחה first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is
that he prays the afternoon prayer and afterward
prays the additional prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the disagreement in favor of מנחה first.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן rules that מנחה precedes מוסף.

steps.title: רבי זירא sits by the בית מדרש
steps.stepSummary: When tired from learning, רבי זירא sits at the doorway so he can stand for passing חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא grew tired from his studies, he would go and sit at the doorway of רבי נתן בר טובי’s place. He said: When the רבנן pass, I will stand before them and receive reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story that sets up another report of the ruling. It explains why רבי זירא is sitting near the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא is too tired to continue studying, but he can still honor passing חכמים by standing. Being at the doorway also places him where he can hear news from the בית מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage sitting at the doorway.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה חֲלִישׁ מִגִּירְסֵיהּ
phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira grew tired from his studies,
he would go and sit

phrases.aramaic: אַפִּתְחָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר טוֹבִי.
phrases.english: at the doorway of Rabbi Natan bar Tovi’s place.
He said: When the Sages pass,
then I will stand before them and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא כִּי הֲוָה חֲלִישׁ מִגִּירְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story begins that will give another report about the same תפילה-order dispute.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks what was taught
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר טובי comes out, and רבי זירא asks whose ruling was stated in the בית מדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר טובי came out. He said to him: Who stated a הלכה in the בית מדרש?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר טובי reaches the doorway, and רבי זירא asks about the ruling just taught inside. The question sets up the report that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story now moves from why רבי זירא is at the doorway to what he learns there. His question seeks the source of the ruling heard in the בית מדרש.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who comes out and answers.

phrases.aramaic: נְפַק אֲתָא רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר טוֹבִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Tovi came out and arrived,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן אֲמַר הֲלָכָה בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: and he asked him: Who stated a halakha in the study hall?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן אֲמַר הֲלָכָה בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The doorway setting leads to רבי זירא’s question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who stated the ruling in the בית מדרש?

steps.title: The ruling is reported in the negative
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר טובי reports that רבי יוחנן said the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה’s order of מוסף before מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, who says that a person prays מוסף and afterward prays מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר טובי answers רבי זירא by reporting רבי יוחנן’s ruling. This report states which view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יוחנן stated the preferred order directly: מנחה before מוסף. Here the same result is expressed by saying that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, who puts מוסף first.
steps.whatToRemember: The direct ruling and this negative report agree: מנחה comes before מוסף.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda,
who says that a person prays the additional prayer
and afterward prays the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers רבי זירא’s question and restates the result of the earlier dispute in negative form.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן stated that the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה’s מוסף-first order.

steps.title: Did he say the ruling himself?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא checks whether the ruling just reported was stated by רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: Did רבי יוחנן say it?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing the ruling in step 37, רבי זירא asks רבי נתן בר טובי to confirm its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about attribution, not about what the ruling says. רבי זירא wants to know whether he can confidently name רבי יוחנן as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage whose attribution is being checked

phrases.english: He said to him: Did Rabbi Yoḥanan say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַמְרַהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the attribution of the ruling reported in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן himself stated the ruling.

steps.title: The attribution is confirmed
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר טובי answers yes, and the ruling is repeated forty times to fix it in memory.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: Yes. He learned it from him forty times.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר טובי confirms the attribution. The account adds that the teaching was learned repeatedly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer settles רבי זירא’s immediate question. The forty repetitions show how carefully the attribution was retained.

keyTerms.meaning: learned or repeated it from him

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
He learned it from him forty times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי יוחנן’s attribution.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes; the teaching was learned repeatedly.

steps.title: Why did this teaching matter so much to you?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר טובי asks whether the teaching is especially important to רבי זירא because it is singular or because it is new to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: Is it the only one you have, or is it new to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר טובי asks why רבי זירא gave this teaching such attention. He offers two possible explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not another question about the law. It asks why רבי זירא was so focused on learning and confirming this particular attribution.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it a singular teaching for you,
or is it new to you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדָא הִיא לָךְ, אוֹ חֲדַת הִיא לָךְ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the confirmed teaching received so much attention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי זירא’s interest came from the teaching being singular for him or from its being new to him.

steps.title: The attribution was new to him
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the information is new because he had been unsure about its connection to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: It is new to me, because I was uncertain about רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains his interest: he had been uncertain whether to attribute this ruling to רבי יוחנן or to רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The uncertainty was about who said the ruling. The confirmation in step 39 resolves that uncertainty for רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage involved in the attribution uncertainty

phrases.english: He said to him: It is new to me,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּמְסַפְּקָא לִי בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: because I was uncertain about Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲדַת הִיא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Chooses the second explanation: the attribution was new to רבי זירא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He had been uncertain whether the ruling belonged to רבי יהושע בן לוי.

steps.title: A warning about praying the additional prayer late
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי applies a verse to someone who prays מוסף after seven hours according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: For anyone who prays מוסף after seven hours, according to רבי יהודה, the פסוק says, ‘Those afflicted because of the appointed time I gathered from you; they were.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי about late מוסף. It sets up the next question: what does the quoted verse mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven-hour limit is stated according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהושע בן לוי applies a verse of criticism to prayer after that time, and the גמרא will examine the verse’s wording.

keyTerms.meaning: words of the verse applied to missing an appointed time

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who prays the additional prayer
after seven hours, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
about him Scripture says:
‘Those afflicted because of the appointed time I gathered from you; they were.’

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the attribution discussion to a separate teaching by רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה’s time limit, a verse of criticism is applied to one who prays מוסף after seven hours.

steps.title: How does the verse suggest destruction?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word נוּגֵי can carry the meaning needed for the warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows that this word, נוגי, is an expression of destruction?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to check the meaning of one word in the verse. This question prepares the explanation of רבי יהושע בן לוי’s quotation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning depends on reading נוּגֵי as a word of harm or destruction. The גמרא asks for support for that reading.

phrases.english: What shows that this word ‘nugei’
is an expression of destruction?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי נוּגֵי לִישָּׁנָא דִתְבָרָא הוּא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the verse quoted in step 42 fits its warning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Evidence that נוּגֵי can mean destruction.

steps.title: A translation supports the reading of destruction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites רב יוסף’s translation, which speaks of destruction for delaying appointed times.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף translated: Destruction comes upon the enemies of the house of Israel because they delayed the times of the festivals in Jerusalem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רב יוסף’s translation of the verse. His wording connects a delayed appointed time with destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The translation supplies the meaning asked for in step 43. It also explains why a verse about an appointed time was brought into the discussion of late מוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: the appointed times of the festivals

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef translated:

phrases.aramaic: תְּבָרָא אָתֵי עַל שָׂנְאֵיהוֹן דְּבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: Destruction comes upon the enemies of the house of Israel
because they delayed the appointed times of the festivals
in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִמְתַרְגֵּם רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the requested support for reading נוּגֵי as destruction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף’s translation uses destruction when explaining the verse’s delayed appointed times.

steps.title: A warning about praying the morning prayer late
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר applies the same verse to שחרית prayed after four hours according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: For anyone who prays שחרית after four hours, according to רבי יהודה, the פסוק says, ‘Those in sorrow because of the appointed time I gathered from you; they were.’
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר brings a parallel statement about late שחרית. He quotes the same verse, but the following discussion reads נוּגֵי as sorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer and time limit have changed: the case is now שחרית after four hours according to רבי יהודה. The גמרא next checks the meaning of the verse for this use.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage who gives the parallel statement

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Anyone who prays the morning prayer
after four hours, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
about him Scripture says:
‘Those in sorrow because of the appointed time I gathered from you; they were.’

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a parallel application of the same verse, now concerning late שחרית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה’s time limit, the verse is applied to one who prays שחרית after four hours.

steps.title: How does the verse suggest sorrow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for support for reading נוּגֵי as an expression of sorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: What shows that this word, נוגי, is an expression of sorrow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again checks the key word in the verse. This time it asks whether נוּגֵי can mean sorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question follows רבי אלעזר’s use of the verse. His reading needs evidence for sorrow, rather than the earlier reading of destruction.

phrases.english: What shows that this word ‘nugei’
is an expression of sorrow?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי נוּגֵי לִישָּׁנָא דְצַעֲרָא הוּא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for the meaning of the verse in רבי אלעזר’s statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Evidence that נוּגֵי can express sorrow.

steps.title: Another verse connects the word to sorrow
steps.stepSummary: A verse about a soul weighed down by sorrow supports the proposed meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: ‘My soul drips from sorrow.’
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting another verse. Its related word, מִתּוּגָה, refers to sorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer uses similar wording from another verse to explain נוּגֵי. That gives רבי אלעזר’s reading textual support.

phrases.english: As it is written:
‘My soul drips from sorrow.’

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״דָּלְפָה נַפְשִׁי מִתּוּגָה״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a verse supporting the reading of נוּגֵי as sorrow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The related word מִתּוּגָה appears in a verse describing sorrow.

steps.title: A second verse supports the meaning of sorrow
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another verse in which נוּגוֹת appears alongside bitterness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The evidence is from here: ‘Her young women are sorrowful, and she is bitter.’
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a second source for the meaning of נוּגֵי. His verse places a closely related word next to bitterness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This does not change the rule about late שחרית. It strengthens the explanation of the word used in רבי אלעזר’s verse.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
From here:
